verdict: Clean, consistent card with a clear lime primary and a proper title and x, but it is a generic pause-menu clone that carries no pad-lost context, and it has a bare black background, a stray top-tab, small type and an unevenly weighted button stack.

findings.what: The screen is titled 'pad lost' but nothing tells the player which pad or player dropped (p1 vs p2) and there is no pad glyph. The card is the same generic pause menu with a different title, so the actual event is not communicated. The primary 'reconnect' also gives no live key/pad hint.
findings.fix: Add a 32px pad glyph (or a 'player 1' label in tx-2 at 16px) beside the title, and show the live prompt on the reconnect button (e.g. 'reconnect  [a]' at 16px, acc-ink).

findings.what: The raid or hub is fully gone, leaving a flat #0b0c0d void with a tiny 480x485 card (about 25% of the width). It feels empty and unfinished compared with the 90% centred card order (Q43) used by other windows, and nothing shows the game is paused behind it.
findings.fix: Keep the frozen game frame behind it under a rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim, or make the card follow the window rule. Either way, drop the pure-black void.

findings.what: The pause menu is five levels deep: a lime fill, two full-width outlined rows, a 2-up row, and a red text-only link. 'report a problem', 'feedback' and 'what's new' compete with the real recovery action on a pad-lost screen and add clutter. 'end run' reads as plain text, not a button, and has no pad-focus affordance.
findings.fix: Keep only reconnect, settings and end run here. Move feedback, report and what's new to the normal pause menu. Give 'end run' a 1px --danger border at the same 56px height.

findings.what: Button labels render at about 18px, below the 20px body size, and are thin against the 56px rows, so the label weight is far lighter than the row it sits in. From a couch the secondary labels are weak.
findings.fix: Set button text to 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Keep 16px for hints only.

findings.what: The 36px accent tab at the top-left corner is dim olive and sits outside the 24px padding axis, so it looks like a rendering glitch rather than a deliberate marker. It is only on this panel's top edge, not aligned with the title text.
findings.fix: Draw it at full --acc, 2px tall, starting at x=760 (the content edge), or remove it.

findings.what: The close x sits at 1136 while the right content edge is 1160, so it is not aligned with the button column. The title baseline and the x centre are also off by a few px. The header divider is the only element on a 1px line.
findings.fix: Right-align the x glyph to x=1160 with a 40px hit box centred on the title's vertical midline (y=349).

findings.what: The gap between the lowest button and 'end run' is 44px and the bottom padding is 60px, against 16px between the buttons above, so the rhythm breaks and the bottom feels heavy. The 2-up row gap is 16px, which matches, but the outer card padding is 40px, not the 24px token.
findings.fix: Use 24px between the last button and end run, 24px bottom padding, and 24px card padding on the 8px grid.

findings.what: Only the lime fill shows focus. Nothing shows what happens on a d-pad move: the idle rows have the same 1px grey border, and the focus treatment for the other rows is not visible here, so there is no sign of the pad-focus style (raised fill plus lime bar).
findings.fix: Give a focused secondary row --ui-raised fill, a 3px --acc left bar and a tx-1 label; keep the primary as lime fill, so it is clear which row is selected.
